coaching.coaching: Pin down presence-check behaviour of the stdlib credential carrier with a concrete worked example.
coaching.subject: presence-check behaviour of the stdlib credential carrier

metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add an acceptance criterion that the operation-binding tests prove accurate credential presence checks (set vs absent), matching the repair plan's 'accurate presence checks' deliverable.
evidence: Repair plan: 'Preserve credential hiding from repr/equality/hash, exact reveal at adapter authentication, and accurate presence checks.'
ACs cover repr/equality/hash absence and reveal() exactness but omit presence checks
findings.finding: The repair plan requires the stdlib credential carrier to preserve 'accurate presence checks', but no acceptance criterion verifies presence-check behavior, whereas repr/equality/hash and reveal() each have covering ACs.
scenarios: A regression in presence detection (e.g. empty vs set credential) ships unverified because no AC exercises it
findings.suggested_fix: Add AC: 'Operation-binding tests prove presence checks correctly report whether a credential is set vs absent.'

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm the stdlib credential carrier preserves the serialization/JSON-rendering masking that ADR 0098 (R20, §4) attributes to SecretStr — not only repr/equality/hash — or record that the runtime never serializes StaticAuth so the guarantee is not load-bearing.
evidence: docs/adr/0098-...md:183-189: 'use a provider-specific, non-serializable static auth container backed by Pydantic SecretStr ... Pydantic masks normal string/repr and default JSON rendering ... RP-04 therefore also excludes the secret field from ... serialization.'
R20 (line 541-543) cites SecretStr's representation/serialization behavior as the established prior art the container relies on.
Plan's preserved-behavior list stops at repr/equality/hash + reveal + presence; serialization masking is not named.
search of runtime.py for 'json' returns no matches, so the runtime itself does not serialize — lowering (but not eliminating) exposure risk.
findings.finding: The plan replaces Pydantic SecretStr with a stdlib carrier and enumerates preserving repr/equality/hash hiding, exact reveal, and presence checks, but omits the serialization/JSON-rendering masking that ADR 0098 (R20, §4) explicitly attributes to SecretStr as a distinct capability ('Pydantic masks normal string/repr and default JSON rendering').
findings.location: Repair plan, first bullet ('Replace the Pydantic SecretStr dependency ... with a frozen stdlib credential carrier. Preserve credential hiding from repr/equality/hash, exact reveal ..., and accurate presence checks.')
scenarios: A stdlib carrier whose default __dict__/asdict/JSON encoding surfaces the raw secret if any future consumer serializes StaticAuth, since dataclass fields are still readable via astuple/asdict even when compare=False/repr=False.
A reviewer relying on the ADR's SecretStr guarantee assumes serialization masking survives the swap.
findings.suggested_fix: Add serialization/JSON-rendering masking (and asdict/astuple exposure) to the enumerated preserved behaviors, and add a behavioral canary asserting the raw credential never appears in any serialized/asdict form of StaticAuth.
